text:
alex_k: quick heads-up — seeing 6–12ms extra host-side on small requests (seq<=32). investigation suggests most of it is tokenization + request parse + grpc/http write overhead :eyes:

maria_s: can you paste the flame? curious if kernel selection or batching heuristics show up as hot

alex_k: pasted a tiny profile snapshot from a p95 trace:
```
flame: host-side p95 (small requests)
+6.2ms  tokenization (utf8 decode + regex split)
+3.1ms  parse_request (proto unpack + header validation)
+2.4ms  grpc/writev (http2 HPACK + small writes)
+0.5ms  kv-cache lookup (miss penalties)
```

kevin_p: hmm kv-cache only 0.5ms but we see tail spikes when kv shards hot. could be contention causing jitter, not avg cost

jordan_t: are these requests using dedicated kernel path (faster matmul) or falling back to generic? kernel selection could affect CPU wakeups if sequence length switching triggers recompile?

alex_k: mostly same model variant, so runtime chooses same kernel. i instrumented kernel-selection latency and it's ~50–100us, so not the main culprit. this is pre-inference host overhead.

maria_s: OK. two hypotheses: (1) tokenization regex/alloc churn — optimize to streaming tokenizer; (2) gRPC small-write path — writev + HPACK for many small frames. either can add ms at p95

kevin_p: i ran a microbench: single-threaded tokenizer (current) vs streaming tokenizer patch. streaming wins ~4ms on 32-token payloads. patch available in branch: `ingress/smol-token-stream`

alex_k: nice. also tried coalescing small gRPC writes by buffering up to 512B per call; that saved ~1.5ms p95 but increases jitter on large payloads. tradeoff.

ingress-bot: deploy check — canary config for `ingress/smol-token-stream` passes unit + integration tests (mock-gRPC). no lint errors.

maria_s: what about batching heuristics? if we wait to batch tiny requests we improve GPU efficiency but add latency. maybe a hybrid: immediate passthrough for <50ms host cost, otherwise autobatch as before

kevin_p: propose: if predicted host overhead > threshold (measured per route), route through an "ingress-fastpath" that uses streaming tokenizer + write coalesce + bypass certain header checks (safe for verified customers). else standard path with batching hints to runtime.

alex_k: sounds good. i have perf numbers from a small canary: fastpath reduces p95 from 18.4ms -> 11.2ms on seq<=32 for hosted API, and tail error rate unchanged.

jordan_t: we should also check KV cache behavior under the fastpath. coalescing may change request arrival patterns and cause kvcache thrash. can you run kvcache stress with the canary traces?

kevin_p: on it. initial runs show a slight increase in eviction rate (+3%) but no effect on hit latency. will run longer window.

maria_s: next steps:
- alex_k to open PR with streaming tokenizer + coalesce write option (small, opt-in)
- kevin_p to run extended kvcache stress + p99 tail test
- jordan_t to add a tiny kernel-selection probe to rule out any fallback jitter (50us resolution)

alex_k: created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/628 (draft). patch toggled behind feature flag `ingress.fastpath_small_requests` :thumbsup:

kevin_p: i'll schedule a 2h kvcache run tonight and post results tomorrow morning

jordan_t: if kvcache looks stable, we can flip flag for limited customers and monitor CPU tail + latency. also add a trace to the console dashboard for host_preproc_ms per-route

maria_s: great. also log note: watch for http1 vs http2 clients — coalesce helps http1 smallwrites more than http2 because of HPACK overhead differences. include that in rollout notes.

alex_k: thanks all. will follow up in the PR with benchmark artifacts and a short runbook for canarying.

ingress-bot: reminder — please add a short changelog entry when merging (component: ingress, area: perf, risk: medium)
